title: A bank account class
description:
Write a class `Account` with a metatable whose `__index` is the class itself:

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `Account.new(owner, balance)` | a new account; `balance` defaults to 0 |
| `acc:deposit(amount)` | adds the amount and returns the new balance; an amount of 0 or less raises an error containing `amount must be positive` |
| `acc:withdraw(amount)` | takes the amount out and returns the new balance; an amount of 0 or less raises the same error; more than the balance raises an error containing `insufficient funds` and changes nothing |
| `acc:balance()` | the balance |
| `acc:history()` | a list of strings, one per successful deposit or withdrawal, oldest first: `"deposit 50"`, `"withdraw 20"` |
| `tostring(acc)` | `"Account(Ada, 130)"` |

Each account has its own balance and history.

solution.solution.lua:
Account = {}
Account.__index = Account

function Account.new(owner, balance)
    local self = setmetatable({}, Account)
    self.owner = owner
    self.money = balance or 0
    self.log = {}
    return self
end

local function check_amount(amount)
    if type(amount) ~= "number" or amount <= 0 then
        error("amount must be positive", 3)
    end
end

function Account:deposit(amount)
    check_amount(amount)
    self.money = self.money + amount
    self.log[#self.log + 1] = "deposit " .. amount
    return self.money
end

function Account:withdraw(amount)
    check_amount(amount)
    if amount > self.money then error("insufficient funds", 2) end
    self.money = self.money - amount
    self.log[#self.log + 1] = "withdraw " .. amount
    return self.money
end

function Account:balance()
    return self.money
end

function Account:history()
    local copy = {}
    for i, entry in ipairs(self.log) do copy[i] = entry end
    return copy
end

function Account.__tostring(acc)
    return "Account(" .. acc.owner .. ", " .. acc.money .. ")"
end

hints: `Account.__index = Account` sends a missing key, such as a method name, from an account to the class.
Call the data field something other than the method's name: an account with a field called `balance` would hide the `balance` method.
unitTests:
test("new accounts", function()
    local a = Account.new("Ada", 100)
    local b = Account.new("Grace")
    check_eq(a:balance(), 100)
    check_eq(b:balance(), 0)
    check(getmetatable(a) == Account, "an account's metatable is Account")
    check(rawget(a, "deposit") == nil, "methods belong to the class, not to each account")
end)

test("deposits and withdrawals", function()
    local a = Account.new("Ada", 100)
    check_eq(a:deposit(50), 150)
    check_eq(a:withdraw(20), 130)
    check_eq(a:balance(), 130)
    check_eq(a:history(), { "deposit 50", "withdraw 20" })
end)

test("accounts are separate", function()
    local a, b = Account.new("A"), Account.new("B")
    a:deposit(10)
    check_eq(b:balance(), 0)
    check_eq(b:history(), {})
end)

test("bad amounts raise errors", function()
    local a = Account.new("Ada", 50)
    check_error_like("amount must be positive", a.deposit, a, 0)
    check_error_like("amount must be positive", a.withdraw, a, -5)
    check_error_like("insufficient funds", a.withdraw, a, 51)
    check_eq(a:balance(), 50, "a failed withdrawal changes nothing")
    check_eq(a:history(), {})
end)

test("printing", function()
    local a = Account.new("Ada", 100)
    a:deposit(30)
    check_eq(tostring(a), "Account(Ada, 130)")
end)
